root_cause_label: Agent never moves onto the gold cell to trigger the win condition; returns 'pickup' on gold which is a no-op in the engine, so the game loops forever
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a turn() that returns 'pickup' when standing on the gold tile, but the engine's win flag is only set by a movement action that steps onto the gold cell, so the game never terminates; the agent then misattributed the resulting infinite hang to test infrastructure and spent the remaining steps cycling through simplifications and rewrites without ever correcting the fundamental win-condition logic.
t_err_evidence: solution.js created with flawed Stacker logic: shouldDropBlock checks cell.type but carrying state is never tracked
t_commit_evidence: Step 7: agent runs 'node test_runner.js' and the process hangs after printing 'DEBUG: invoking game.run(3)'. The agent cannot obtain any test results and from this point on pursues the incorrect hypothesis that the test infrastructure is broken, never revisiting whether its win-condition logic is correct.
t_surface_evidence: node test_runner.js hangs with no output after 10 seconds, exit code -1, test never completes
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that issuing 'pickup' when cell.type===3 (gold) would constitute a win, without verifying the actual win mechanism in challenge.js. Reading challenge.js reveals that win is set in function z() only when a movement action moves the player onto a type-p cell. The agent never tested or verified this assumption before writing the first solution.
